sentences.text: The animal is known from a single partial skull found in the Melovatskaya Formation of the Volgograd Region in Russia.
Researchers later determined the fossil was an incomplete and abraded skull rather than a brain cast.
The fossil was initially misidentified as a fossilized brain of an enantiornithean bird.
The brain shows unusual characteristics, including a well-developed olfactory system and a large cerebrum.
The genus Cerebavis was described by Kurochkin and colleagues in 2006.
A 2015 reappraisal by the original authors concluded the specimen belonged to an ornithurine rather than an enantiornithean.
The animal was identified as an ornithurine due to the lack of a postorbital bone, thin skull roof, and high fusion between skull bones.
The brain structure resembles that of living birds, lacking a large pineal gland and having olfactory bulbs of expected size.
Despite its advanced shape, the animal seemingly lacked a wulst, suggesting its brain was not fully modern.
The brain could show a relatively large parietal eye and pineal gland.
Cerebavis is classified within the order Saurischia.
The genus belongs to the suborder Theropoda.
Cerebavis is placed in the unranked family Avialae.
The animal is classified within the unranked genus Ornithurae.
The parent group of Cerebavis is Ornithurae.
Cerebavis lived during the middle Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.
The animal lived between 99.6 and 93.5 million years ago during the middle Cenomanian.
A 2021 redescription of Borogovia suggested Cerebavis might be a scansoriopterygid located at the base of the non-avian Oviraptorosauria clade.
In 2011, the specimen was regarded as potentially a nomen dubium.
It is debated whether the animal is an ornithurine or a scansoriopterygid at the base of non-avian Oviraptorosauria.
